## Scope and defaults

`apps/contacts/cloudflare` is an additive TanStack Start, Vite+ and Void
candidate for `<app>.tutur3u.com` in the `tutur3u.com` zone.
Contacts hosts tutoring workspaces. Existing Contacts Next.js source, Vercel
routing and customer behavior remain canonical. This PR does not deploy,
provision, attach hostnames, change DNS or enable production publication.

`CONTACTS_START_CANDIDATE` defaults to `off`; only the exact value `staging`
on the exact HTTPS staging origin admits requests. Unset, unknown and disabled
values return 503 without invoking Start or calling Next. Worker-first assets,
no SPA fallback, disabled workers.dev/preview URLs and no routes prevent an
asset or public-host bypass. The configuration contains no credentials, fallback
origin, bindings, schedules, queues or database migrations.

The only native route is GET/HEAD `/__contacts1`, an inert JSON probe. All
customer pages, route handlers, public assets and other methods use Next fallback.
`start-route-manifest.json` records the full route census, local owners,
rewrites, Web API fallback and the non-Contacts workspace redirect. The generated
private census artifact additionally traces inherited layouts/templates, actions,
`after()`, `connection()` and cache boundaries through first-party imports.
Unresolved import edges remain blockers for later native slices.

## Preserve identity and API ownership

The candidate forwards through `@tuturuuu/start-bridge/api-forward` to a separately
admitted Contacts **Next staging** origin. It does not dispatch `/api/*` directly
to Web: existing Contacts feedback, payment/billing and auth handlers must win;
the remaining workspace API rewrites and `/api/:path*` fallback retain Web as owner.
There is no new Next catch-all or route-segment rendering configuration.

Contacts Next middleware retains app-session audience/expiry, MFA, refresh,
workspace ownership, locale redirects and non-migrated-route redirects. Native
code never resolves a user. Future native slices must use an injected Contacts
satellite session via `getSatelliteAppSessionUser('contacts')`, never
`user-helper`. Shared domain libraries remain independent of React/router/runtime.

EN and VI use `localePrefix: never`. Explicit locale prefixes redirect to the
unprefixed path and set `NEXT_LOCALE`; the candidate must preserve those redirects,
cookies, query strings and reload behavior.

Forwarding preserves authorization, cookies, request bodies, Next action headers,
streaming, abort signals, statuses, retry headers and separate response cookies.
It signs the Cloudflare client IP, removes spoofable forwarding headers and
hop-by-hop nominations, and never retries a failed write. The Next origin must
attest the pinned staging Supabase project before its response is released.
Duplicate Domain attributes or non-staging cookie domains reject the whole
response. Internal redirects return through Contacts staging; issuer redirects
must target the separately configured central staging login.

## Owner inputs blocking contacts.staging

`cloudflare/staging.env.example` is a dormant template. The release owner must
supply and privately verify all of the following before publication:

- Scoped Cloudflare staging account/token, Worker identity, private admission and
  separately authorized hostname, DNS/TLS and ingress topology.
- Immutable Contacts Next staging fallback with verified team, project, deployment,
  source SHA and staging Supabase identity attestation. The Vercel hostname filter
  alone does not establish team/project ownership; never forward credentials until
  that ownership is verified. Keep fallback and Worker origins distinct.
- Staging Supabase publishable/server keys, schema, callbacks, disposable actor,
  workspace and Contacts tutoring/feedback/module fixtures. The expected public
  staging ref is pinned in `profile.ts`; it is not a credential.
- Staging-only `TRUSTED_PROXY_ORIGIN_SECRET` and matching Next proxy configuration.
  Compare private SHA-256 fingerprints with production before enablement and after
  either key rotates: equal or unavailable fingerprints hold publication.
- Central Web staging auth/API service, Contacts app-session keys/audience and
  allowlists, exact `.staging.tutur3u.com` Secure cookie support across issuer,
  Contacts and Supabase adapters, MFA and refresh callbacks. Those hosted adapters
  are prerequisites; this candidate does not silently enable staging auth in Next.
- Staging R2/storage, Turnstile, email/OAuth and payment sandbox inputs required by
  the existing Next flows; never production credentials or real payment data.
- Exact source/artifact identity, independent security review, applicable CI
  lint/types/tests/build, emitted Worker receipt and hosted EN/VI acceptance.

Secrets stay in the approved secret store. Neither `.env` credentials nor browser
traces, screenshots, passwords or raw handoff URLs belong in public artifacts.

## Verification and controls

Use a remote build host under `ttr resources`; do not build on the local hub. From the repository root:

```bash
bun run --cwd apps/contacts routes:candidate:check
bun run --cwd apps/contacts test:candidate
bun run --cwd apps/contacts test:staging:policy
bun run --cwd apps/contacts type-check:candidate
bun run --cwd apps/contacts test:candidate:controls
bun run --cwd apps/contacts build:candidate
bun run --cwd apps/contacts test:candidate:runtime
bun check:changed
```

`routes:candidate` regenerates the tracked manifest. `--artifact <private-path>`
adds the import/boundary census. The control runner temporarily removes admission,
then forces all requests into Start. It requires assertion failures for both,
restores the source in `finally`, and reruns the original suite green.
The emitted runtime uses workerd through Wrangler's pinned Miniflare supplier,
with outbound requests confined to a synthetic Next fixture. It proves the
actual emitted gate, native probe, fallback and immediate disable behavior;
it does not prove hosted identity or database access.

The validation-only candidate CI has no publisher or secrets and retains the
repository's CI admission gate. No admission label is added by this lane.

The hosted Playwright suite is intentionally dormant. Set the names below in
the approved secret environment, then run `test:e2e:staging` on an allowed host:

- `CONTACTS_STAGING_SOURCE_SHA` (full emitted/deployed source SHA).
- `CONTACTS_STAGING_SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF` (the pinned staging ref).
- `CONTACTS_STAGING_DISPOSABLE_ACCOUNT=confirmed`.
- `CONTACTS_STAGING_EMAIL`, `CONTACTS_STAGING_PASSWORD`, `CONTACTS_STAGING_USER_ID`,
  `CONTACTS_STAGING_WORKSPACE_ID` for the disposable fixture.
- Optional `CONTACTS_STAGING_BASE_URL` and `CONTACTS_STAGING_WEB_ORIGIN` accept only
  the exact Contacts and issuer staging origins; canonical/prod/confusable hosts
  are rejected before browser launch.

Both locales exercise real login handoff, exact build identity, actor read via
the Web API proxy, Secure cookie continuity, app-session refresh, tutoring,
feedback, attendance and posts navigation, plus reloads. The network fence blocks
production, non-auth mutations and unexpected WebSockets. This read-only suite
does not establish editor writes, payments, MFA recovery or wrong-audience denials;
those require separately reviewed disposable hosted cases before a customer slice.

## Cost, stop and later cutover

Disabled requests perform zero downstream calls; admitted probes do the same.
Each fallback performs at most one downstream call, with zero application retries,
no persistence and no rescheduling. Source tests count calls for repeated failures
and disable transitions. There is no background actor to survive the stop fence.
The durable deployment setting `CONTACTS_START_CANDIDATE=off` stops new work;
remove/disable only this candidate Worker if unexpected serving persists, preserve
receipts and the Next rollback artifact, and verify zero new downstream calls.
Ingress/CPU limits alone do not cap aggregate request spend. Before exposing ingress,
the owner must admit finite acceptance volume and verify provider topology and
hosted stop behavior. This PR does not claim a total-spend cap or hosted stop proof.

The product decision is web first, then per-app staging acceptance followed by
automatic cutover with immediate rollback. This PR prepares Contacts only; it
contains no cutover controller, one-origin routing or publication authority.
A later owner must prove session/API parity, customer tutoring/editor flows,
bounded cost/stop behavior and exact source receipts, then execute the authorized
promotion/rollback procedure. Disabling a future native route cohort must restore
Next immediately; disabling this entire staging candidate returns 503 and leaves
the existing canonical Next app serving customers.
